title: He Walked Out on His Clan After Cutting a Seven-Star Knight . . . (Part 8)
caption:
In The Swordmaster's Youngest Son, Jin Runcandel slices a seven-star knight's jaw as his own sword shatters, then tells his father he is leaving the clan.
In the Arkhin Kingdom he beats down a crooked innkeeper and walks into a criminal auction house tied to the curse on his sword.

Follow for Part 9!

#swordmastersyoungestson #manhwarecap #manhwa #regression #fyp
credit: Swordmaster's Youngest Son (Hwangze Penguin / Mr. Big / AZI)
comment: Jetu tried to sell Jin and his crew at a criminal auction, and Jin chose to keep him alive. Was that mercy or a mistake? Why?

segments.say: Jin's sword shatters in mid-swing, yet his last cut still slices a seven-star knight across the *jaw*. Then Jin drops like a rock.
To see how it got here, go back to the arena, where Jin is busy *demolishing* a poet.
Bubarre wants to introduce himself first. Jin says shut your mouth, and punches him mid-sentence, right in the *face*.
Jin keeps hitting until the poet screams that it is *over*. The crowd cheers like it is a Netflix special.
But the poet already surrendered, and Jin grabs him for round two. Margiela begs her brother Bishkel to *step in*.
Bishkel strolls in and says fight me instead. He is a *seven-star* knight, and Jin just looks bored.
Jin remembers this poet from his past life, arrested as a dangerous *transfigurator*. So why is a seven-star knight protecting him?
That mystery can wait. Bishkel fights like a cunning snake, and Jin's clan fights like a charging *rhino*.
One clash, and Jin is pushed back, shirt in ribbons, blood on his chest. Five-star versus seven-star. *Ouch*.
Then Jin feels the *sensation* from his past life. Blue light rolls off him, and Bishkel stops smiling.
Their blades meet one last time. Jin's sword shatters, and the arena goes *silent*.
Bishkel touches his jaw. There is a thin red cut he never saw *coming*.
If Jin had been a tenth of a second faster, Bishkel would have *lost*. Instead, Jin collapses.
Not bad for a loss. Even Bishkel admits Jin is someone to watch out *for*.
Two days later, Jin wakes up with Murakhan the cat sitting on his *face*. He yanks the cat off, and the banquet is over.
The castle will not stop talking about the fight. Jin credits Luna's eyes-closed lessons for the Blade of the *Heart*.
But he can only trigger it at the brink. Not exactly a reliable *weapon*.
Then Siris sends snow flowers, which mean the unending fight. Gilly calls it romance. Jin calls it a *rematch*.
The patriarch wants him right now, so Jin walks into the crypt that night and says he is leaving the *clan*.
The first patriarch was never buried in the Garden of Swords, because of the dark *power* Jin carries.
A humiliating pact with the Zeifls cursed the bloodline, so every Runcandel born since is unable to use *mana*.
Jin admits he lied about why he wanted the shadow force. Dad asks if he will take the clan. Jin says he will see the world first, then maybe *take it*.
His father laughs and gives him five years to find his answer. Classic Runcandel family *therapy*.
Gilly waits outside with a trunk and Murakhan. Jin says a nanny ruins his reputation, and she wins by simply not *leaving*.
They walk out, and the five-year clock starts *ticking*. Back in the crypt, the patriarch admits Jin is the clan's only hope.
Reserve flagbearers build a name alone, and catching *villains* is the fastest way. Dad gave Jin five years, not two.
First stop is the Arkhin Kingdom. Jin remembers an underground auction house there, but clan rules let him carry only ten gold *coins*.
Jin tells Murakhan to transform. Gilly panics that people might see, but the cat turns into a giant *dragon* anyway.
Back at the castle, Luna spots the dragon and wishes her little brother luck, even though he left without saying *goodbye*.
The flight leaves Gilly puking in the Jian Kingdom. Murakhan blames Jin, and Jin blames the wild *flying*.
Murakhan watches Gilly while Jin goes for money, and he finds Sember, a noble who never got to thank the man who saved his *life*.
Jin clamps a hand over Sember's mouth and says he is that man. Then he orders jewelry and cash. Jin calls it a favor. Sember's face calls it a *mugging*.
Most reserve flagbearers start out broke, but Jin has Sember's *gold*. So they feast, and Murakhan wolfs down a whole roast.
Gilly admits she expected to starve. Yesterday she called it extortion, and Jin insists it was *not*.
Murakhan offers to fly everywhere, but most dragons now serve the Zeifls, so that means *war*. He sulks that riffraff rule the skies.
At the portal, Jin hands over clan-forged papers as Jin Grey and Gilly Pitten, two tourists on *holiday*. They fool the whole task force.
They arrive in the Arkhin Kingdom, where Jin spent the last year of his past life. It already looks *miserable*, and everyone blames Tessing, the criminal gang.
Murakhan whines about the *wreck* of an inn, but in they go. The innkeeper, Jetu, grins like a used-car salesman and hands them free orange juice.
The juice is drugged, so by morning they would be at the underground auction house. Murakhan *smashes* the glass into Jetu's face.
A stomp, a whack, and Jetu is on his knees. A dark aura rises, and he hears the words, you *die*.
Jetu begs to talk it over. Murakhan says talk to my boot, and the boot does the *talking*.
Jin knows this crook. In his past life Jetu swindled him out of everything he *owned*. This time, Jin will use him.
Murakhan keeps pounding Jetu until Jin says enough. Jin offers a *deal*. Tell the truth and live, lie and die.
Jetu spills everything. He runs the inn, swindles people, and might be mixed up in human *trafficking*.
Jetu was taking them to the Tessing underground auction house. Jin says be specific, and something *cracks*.
Gilly and Murakhan want Jetu gone, but Jin keeps him alive as a guide. Mercy is a *risky* hobby.
Alone in front of a mirror, Jetu realizes betraying them means *death*. That night, he leads them to a mansion with iron gates and says they are his guests.
Inside, it looks like a palace, with chandeliers, violins, and masks for everyone. Tessing's public face is a man named Salka, but the real boss is Spider-Hand *Aloo*.
Aloo is a seven-star martial artist, and rumor says he has ties to the pureblood Runcandels across the *sea*.
Jin freezes. In his past life, someone cursed him with the Blade's Delusion, a curse that kills any chance of mastering the *sword*.
He spent fifteen years hunting that curse, and Aloo is the first *link* he has found.
Jin's eyes glow behind the mask. They came to wreck Tessing anyway, so why not find Aloo? But what if the man who cursed him shares his last *name*?
